E-trikes and e-quads are now barred from some of Metro Manila’s busiest roads. Starting January 2, 2026, light electric vehicles are no longer allowed on EDSA, C5, Roxas Boulevard, and the Quirino–Magallanes stretch of SLEX. The Land Transportation Office has begun enforcing the ban, with fines and possible impounding now in place.

The agency says these major roads are built for faster, heavier vehicles, and mixing lightweight electric units with high-speed traffic poses safety risks to all road users.

For many Filipinos, these units are daily work tools. They are used by food sellers, water refilling stations, laundry shops, and online sellers that rely on short city trips. The ban introduces new route limits and possible added costs for micro-entrepreneurs who shifted to electric units to save on fuel and maintenance. Some may need to take longer routes or return to fuel-powered vehicles, which can gradually push delivery fees up.

(Report by radar Business)
